messages:
alice.w: quick Q — i'm updating a terraform PR that tweaks Karpenter provisioner for the event-ingestion svc. HPA will scale pods from 2→50 during spike tests but nodes don't show up fast enough, we see ~30s+ queueing and some dropped messages. PR here: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/512

alice.w: current HPA manifest i pasted below for context:
```yaml
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: event-ingestion-hpa
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: Deployment
    name: event-ingestion
  minReplicas: 2
  maxReplicas: 50
  metrics:
  - type: Resource
    resource:
      name: cpu
      target:
        type: Utilization
        averageUtilization: 60
```

alice.w: and the Karpenter provisioner in the PR is basically default with consolidation enabled:
```yaml
apiVersion: karpenter.sh/v1alpha5
kind: Provisioner
metadata:
  name: default
spec:
  consolidation:
    enabled: true
  ttlSecondsUntilExpired: 900
  requirements:
  - key: node.kubernetes.io/instance-type
    operator: In
    values: [m6i.large, c6i.large]
```

alice.w: i'm juggling VPA in 'off' mode (we set requests manually), and some pods have nodeSelector + tolerations. any quick wins before i merge the TF changes?

bob_k: common quick fixes i've used: reduce HPA scale-up stabilization and add aggressive policies so replicas can jump fast. also temporary disable consolidation while testing to let karpenter bring new nodes quicker.

bob_k: example HPA tweaks:
```yaml
behavior:
  scaleUp:
    stabilizationWindowSeconds: 0
    policies:
    - type: Percent
      value: 200
      periodSeconds: 15
```

bob_k: and on the Provisioner, try lowering ttlSecondsUntilExpired to 300 for test cluster and add a wider instance-type mix (including smaller cheaper instances) so scheduling finds capacity faster. also ensure your taints/tolerations aren't blocking the new nodes.

carol.s: fwiw we saw similar with the realtime pipeline — adding a tiny overprovisioner deployment (cheap spot/cpu-small) that keeps ~2 warm nodes for bursts fixed the drop rate. it's a simple Deployment that runs low-priority pods to occupy capacity. when real pods schedule, they evict those.

carol.s: terraform snippet we used (simplified):
```hcl
resource "kubernetes_deployment" "overprovisioner" {
  metadata { name = "overprovisioner" namespace = "kube-system" }
  spec { replicas = 2 /* tiny */ }
}
```

carol.s: also double-check the HPA metricSource latency — if you're using custom metrics there can be a lag before HPA kicks in. CPU-based is fastest.

alice.w: nice. i can try the HPA behavior + temp ttl down to 300 in the PR, and add the wider instance set. is the overprovisioner something we want in prod or just for canaries?

bob_k: short answer: prod is fine if you pick cheap SKUs and mark pods low-priority (best-effort) + tolerations, so they get evicted first. treat it like a warm pool. we have a doc internal/link-to-warm-nodes — i'll paste later.

david: pinged the infra owners and added a quick checklist:
- reduce HPA stabilizationWindowSeconds to 0 for testing
- add scaleUp policy (percent) for fast jumps
- temporarily set provisioner.consolidation.enabled=false in staging
- add smaller instance types and set ttlSecondsUntilExpired=300
- if still failing, deploy overprovisioner (kube-system)

david: i can run the plan/apply for this if you want. @alice.w do you want staging apply now?

alice.w: yes please, staging first. i'll update the PR with the HPA behavior and the wider instance list.

infra-bot: terraform plan for https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/512
```
+ aws_instance_profile.karpenter (new resource)
+ kubernetes_manifest.provisioner (new resource)
+ kubernetes_horizontal_pod_autoscaler.hpa (updated: behavior block)
0 to destroy, 3 to add, 1 to change
```

bob_k: small nit — add a rollout strategy to the deployment (maxSurge: 1, maxUnavailable: 0) so we don't drop capacity during the prov changes.

alice.w: will add that. thanks all — i'll update PR and request staging apply.

david: thanks — if staging looks good, we can promote to canary with a small percentage traffic shift. :thumbsup:
